grpo_trajectory.interpretation: v5 regressed sharply against the v4 baseline (-35pp) with 62.5% TinyV abstentions. The TinyV false-negative correction overshot: the abstention threshold suppressed too many valid rewards, leaving sum_filtered_rewards at the spurious-reward floor (3.0). v6 must either retune the abstention threshold or drop TinyV in favor of GRPO-VPS step-level supervision (exp1209: +24pp), which is the only positive RL-style result of the milestone.

significant_findings: GRPO-VPS step-level supervision delivers +24pp (70% -> 94%) over outcome-only baseline, validating the Phase-3 thesis that per-step verifier rewards beat outcome-only RL. This is the first head-to-head step-vs-outcome comparison on the same eval set and establishes the dominant Phase-3 RL training signal.

Phase 4 sampler clears 100% BFS-intractable puzzles in exp1210 (n=puzzles, all initial energies nonzero), confirming the search-advantage is genuine rather than an easy-puzzle artifact. This is the headline Phase-4 firm pivot evidence the publication hold required.

SDPO dense-reward distillation is bottlenecked by token coverage (22%) rather than by the energy teacher quality. The student policy's tokenizer/log-prob window does not overlap enough with the teacher's selection space to learn a dense reward, so SDPO regressed -19.61pp. This is a coverage problem, not a teacher problem; the energy_teacher_selection_accuracy itself was healthy.
